context: Tests whether the agent detects the modules of a large Maven multi-module Spring Boot system (four domain modules guests, reservations, housekeeping, billing; a technical platform-common module; an app assembly module; 17 domain tables; 38 route handlers) and splits both diagrams by module inside the two fixed files: docs/use_cases.puml with a @startuml Modules overview plus one @startuml block per module, and docs/entity_model.md with a ## Modules table plus one ## Module: section per module, each with its own Mermaid diagram and the entities it owns. Cross-module foreign keys (reservation to guest, invoice to reservation and guest, cleaning_task and maintenance_request to room) must show up as module dependencies.

checklist.name: Fixed artifact paths only
checklist.description: docs/use_cases.puml, docs/entity_model.md, and at least one docs/use_cases/UC-XXX-*.md exist, and there is NO per-module diagram or entity model file (no other *.puml file under docs/, no docs/entity_model/ folder, no docs/*entity*.md besides docs/entity_model.md)

checklist.name: Module overview diagram
checklist.description: docs/use_cases.puml starts with a @startuml block that shows the modules (as package or similar elements) and the actors linked to them, and contains NO usecase element and no UC-XXX id

checklist.name: One diagram block per domain module
checklist.description: docs/use_cases.puml has, after the overview, one separate @startuml ... @enduml block for each of the four domain modules (guests / guest management, reservations, housekeeping, billing — names may vary in wording), each with its own rectangle and use cases

checklist.name: No technical module
checklist.description: Neither diagram file has a module for platform-common, common, app, audit, or security; the audit_log and flyway_schema_history tables are not documented as entities

checklist.name: Use case in exactly one module
checklist.description: Every UC-XXX id appears as a usecase in exactly one module block of docs/use_cases.puml, and check-in, check-out, booking, and cancellation use cases sit in the reservations module, cleaning and inspection in housekeeping, refund and payment in billing, registration and loyalty redemption in guests

checklist.name: Contiguous ids per module
checklist.description: The UC-XXX ids of each module block form one contiguous range (e.g. UC-001 to UC-004 in the first module, UC-005 onwards in the next), following the order of the modules in the overview

checklist.name: Module dependencies in overview
checklist.description: The overview block draws dependency arrows (..> or similar) between modules that reflect the cross-module foreign keys: at least reservations to guests and billing to reservations; housekeeping to reservations (room) is also expected

checklist.name: Specs match diagram
checklist.description: Every UC-XXX id in docs/use_cases.puml has a matching docs/use_cases/UC-XXX-*.md file and every spec file's id is in the diagram

checklist.name: Modules table in entity model
checklist.description: docs/entity_model.md has a ## Modules section with a table naming each module, its entities, and the modules it depends on; the modules match the module blocks of the use case diagram

checklist.name: Module sections with own ER diagram
checklist.description: docs/entity_model.md has one ## Module: <name> section per domain module, and each section contains its own Mermaid erDiagram block (relationships only, no attributes inside entity blocks) followed by the ### attribute table sections of its entities

checklist.name: Entity owned by one module
checklist.description: Every ### ENTITY section appears exactly once in docs/entity_model.md, in the module that writes it: GUEST, GUEST_ADDRESS, LOYALTY_ACCOUNT, LOYALTY_TRANSACTION in guests; ROOM_TYPE, ROOM, RATE_PLAN, RESERVATION (and RESERVATION_ROOM if modeled) in reservations; HOUSEKEEPER, CLEANING_TASK, INSPECTION, MAINTENANCE_REQUEST in housekeeping; INVOICE, INVOICE_LINE, PAYMENT, REFUND in billing

checklist.name: Cross-module relationships
checklist.description: The billing module's ER diagram contains relationship lines from RESERVATION and GUEST to INVOICE, the housekeeping diagram from ROOM to CLEANING_TASK and MAINTENANCE_REQUEST, and the entities borrowed from other modules are marked as such (e.g. a 'From other modules' line naming the owning module) without a second attribute table

checklist.name: AI Unified Process data types
checklist.description: Attribute tables use only Long, String, Integer, Decimal, Boolean, Date, DateTime, with exactly the 5 columns Attribute | Description | Data Type | Length/Precision | Validation Rules; no VARCHAR, BIGINT, NUMERIC, TEXT, BIGSERIAL, or CHAR(2) appears in the document

checklist.name: Aggregated use cases
checklist.description: The total number of use case spec files is between 12 and 24 — well below the 38 route handlers; room types, rooms, and rate plans are maintained in at most two use cases, not one per endpoint

checklist.name: Actors from roles
checklist.description: The diagrams declare actors derived from SecurityConfig and @PreAuthorize roles (guest, receptionist, housekeeper, supervisor, accountant, manager) plus an unauthenticated visitor and the payment provider and/or a scheduler for the night audit; the same actor has the same name in every block

checklist.name: No secret values
checklist.description: No artifact contains a datasource password or webhook secret value, and the /actuator/health and /api/payments/webhook signature check are not written as use cases of their own
